stories.title: Punjab MPA Hina Parvez Butt defends deleted X post on alleged CCD encounter amid criticism
summary: Punjab lawmaker Hina Parvez Butt on Thursday defended herself after a social media post by her regarding an alleged encounter by Punjab’s Crime Control Department prompted outrage and criticism.
She also took exception to remarks by Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari, saying that she “respectfully disagreed”.
Referring to the remarks, Butt said: “None of my actions or words have ever harmed or embarrassed the Punjab chief minister or the government.

stories.title: Mir Raza murder case: Sindh minister says JIT to be formed as per judicial panel's suggestions
summary: Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar said on Thursday that a joint investigation team (JIT) would be formed as per the recommendations of the judicial commission formed to investigate the circumstances surrounding the murder of Mir Raza Ali.

A judicial commission, formed on the Sindh government’s directives after the family accused police of burying the facts, has declared that Ali’s death was a murder and pointed out lapses by the police during the probe.

Submitted to the government on Oct 15, the report by Sindh High Court judge Justice Omar Sial had recommended forming a JIT under the leadership of DIG Baloch to “balance the need for public accountability with preserving Sindh Police morale and reputation”.

stories.title: PM vows to bring back progress to KP, assails PTI's 'callousness' during its tenures
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday vowed that the federal government, which now runs Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under governor’s rule, would make every effort possible to “bring back” progress to the province.

Emergency amid security challenges The Centre had imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.

In the meeting, the governor — who is now in charge of running the province — assured Naqvi he would enforce all policies of the federal government and work together with the security forces for peace and prosperity of the province.

stories.title: Harry Brook scores fastest double century in ODI history in rampant England's 429-4 against Sri Lanka
summary: An inspired Harry Brook scored the fastest double hundred in ODI history as England piled up 429-4 against Sri Lanka in the tri-series in Rawalpindi on Thursday.
The captain clobbered 10 sixes and 21 fours as England posted a first 400-plus ODI total in Pakistan.
But the day belonged to history-maker Brook, who added 185 runs off just 79 balls with Jacks for the fourth wicket.

stories.title: Common ground
summary: IT appears that the PML-N, echoing the PPP’s recent offer, is also willing to re-engage with the opposition, at least on counterterrorism policy.
It is difficult to see how a credible counterterrorism strategy can be framed when the province on the front line of the fight has just been deprived of its elected government.
Yet the government seems consumed by the hubris of unchecked power, while the opposition, particularly the PTI, continues to act as if agitation alone can yield results.

stories.title: JI, govt to hold talks on Friday to work out plan for meeting between PM Shehbaz, Naeem
summary: Friday’s talks between the two sides’ negotiating committees will take place at Punjab House in Islamabad, where they will also work out a schedule for a proposed meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and JI Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman, the party said.

According to the JI statement, Iqbal, who heads the government’s negotiating committee, informed Baloch that the meeting had initially been planned for Tuesday or Wednesday but was postponed because of the government’s “urgent engagements”.
On Sept 20, the party launched a protest march towards Islamabad, warning that if the government failed to abolish the petroleum levy, the protest could turn into one to oust the government.

stories.title: NCCIA arrests Faisalabad man for alleged Saudi visa fraud via TikTok
summary: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) said on Thursday it has arrested a suspect in Faisalabad for allegedly defrauding citizens through a TikTok account advertising visas for Saudi Arabia.

On Oct 10, NCCIA arrested 281 suspects, including 21 foreign nationals and 20 women, during operations against seven illegal call centres allegedly involved in financial fraud, online harassment and honey-trapping in Lahore.
In September, NCCIA, along with the Federal Investigation Agency, arrested six suspects involved in cyber fraud and financial scams, illegal money exchange and human trafficking across Punjab.

summary: The first and last stay named on the closing map as well. const OPENING_LABELS = ['malir-halt', 'safoora-chowrangi', 'nipa', 'expo-centre', 'islamia-college', 'numaish']; // The red line, traced from example.jpg.

stories.title: Targeted by Trump, International Criminal Court wins top EU rights prize
summary: This month, the United States announced sanctions against the ICC aimed at crippling the day-to-day operations of the court, which tries individuals for war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide.

The win comes after ex-ICC judge Navi Pillay, who also served as UN rights chief, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize this month — a choice Trump slammed as “disgraceful”, arguing the award should have gone to him.
The ICC was among three finalists this year, alongside Tanzania opposition leader Tundu Lissu and twin sisters Taraneh and Romina Rahimi, representing those prosecuted by the Iranian government.

stories.title: President Zardari departs for Germany on 3-day visit to discuss bilateral ties
summary: President Asif Ali Zardari departed for Germany on Thursday on a three-day visit to discuss bilateral ties as the two countries are set to mark the 75th anniversary of their diplomatic relations.
In a statement issued earlier, the Foreign Office (FO) said the president’s visit, scheduled for Oct 22-24, is “part of high-level exchanges between Pakistan and Germany”.

During his visit, President Zardari will hold meetings with his German counterpart Frank-Walter Steinmeier, as well as senior leadership and business leaders, with a “particular focus оп economic and trade cooperation”, FO said.

stories.title: Pakistan, EU agree to strengthen counterterrorism cooperation at multilateral forums
summary: Pakistan and the European Union (EU) have agreed to strengthen cooperation at multilateral forums, including the United Nations, to advance a coherent counterterrorism approach, according to a statement issued by the Foreign Office (FO) on Thursday.
The dialogue comes as Pakistan’s counterterrorism challenge enters a new and more complex phase, with terrorist groups evolving their methods of financing and recruitment.

On Tuesday, an international seminar on Pakistan’s evolving counterterrorism landscape, organised by the Institute of Strategic Studies Islamabad, highlighted the changing methods of terrorist groups, including their financing and recruitment.

stories.title: Faster reforms could triple Pakistan’s incomes by 2050, says World Bank
summary: The report says that following progress on macroeconomic stabilisation, Pakistan has an opportunity to achieve faster and sustained economic growth and create more jobs.
The report finds that higher growth is possible if Pakistan follows the path taken by other successful countries in pursuing ambitious economic reforms.
The report outlines an ambitious set of reforms that could enable Pakistan to attain by 2050 the per capita income levels of countries currently at the upper-middle-income threshold.

stories.title: New Delhi steps up air pollution controls ahead of winter
summary: India began annual measures on Thursday to tackle toxic air pollution in New Delhi, a megacity of 30 million people regularly ranked among the world’s most polluted capitals.

In previous years, such measures have failed to curb pollution, which peaks from November to January, when levels of cancer-causing PM 2.5 microparticles often hit more than 300 micrograms per cubic metre, 20 times the World Health Organisation’s recommended daily maximum.
Last year, pollution levels peaked at 846 micrograms per cubic metre, 56 times the WHO limit.

stories.title: LHC summons Punjab home secretary, Kot Lakhpat jail superintendent in plea seeking release of Imran’s sisters
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Thursday summoned the Punjab home secretary and the superintendent of Kot Lakhpat jail in connection with a petition seeking the release of former prime minister Imran Khan’s three sisters.
It stated that Imran’s sisters remained at Lahore’s Kot Lakhpat jail despite the lapse of the 30-day period of their detention.
In Wednesday’s petition, Shahrez contended that the detention period had expired, but the three sisters remained in custody.

stories.title: Karachi judicial magistrate rejects bail plea of anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan
summary: KARACHI: A local court on Thursday rejected TV anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan’s bail plea in a cybercrime case pertaining to the alleged dissemination of anti-state content.
Earlier this week, Hassan was sent to prison on judicial remand after the NCCIA sought an extension of his physical remand by another eight days.
The court also issued notices to the NCCIA on a bail application filed by Hassan’s defence counsel, Barrister Mian Ali Ashfaq, and fixed the matter for hearing on Oct 21.

stories.title: LHC issues notices to foreign secretary in contempt cases over detention of PTI-linked Pakistanis in UAE
summary: On September 14, the LHC had directed the foreign secretary to process and decide within 15 days representations concerning the detention of two citizens — Syed Salman Raza Zaidi and Muhammad Junaid Jahangir.

The counsel for the petitioners submitted that despite representations having been filed regarding the detention of both citizens before the foreign secretary, the representations had not been processed.

Both petitioners had asked the court to direct that legal and consular assistance be provided to Zaidi and Jahangir, that their judicial records be obtained and that diplomatic-level steps be taken toward their return to Pakistan.

stories.title: International Criminal Court, its senior officials awarded 2026 EU Sakharov Prize
summary: The European Parliament on Thursday awarded its 2026 Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought jointly to the International Criminal Court (ICC) and its senior officials, recognising their work in upholding international law and justice.

By awarding the Sakharov Prize to the International Criminal Court and its officials, Parliament recognises the important work carried out by the Court to uphold international law and justice," said EP President Roberta Metsola, announcing the winners to the full assembly.

Lawmakers have repeatedly called on the European Commission to activate the EU's blocking statute to protect ICC officials from the extraterritorial effects of sanctions and safeguard the court's independence.

stories.title: Salman Akram Raja rejects claims Sohail Afridi derailed talks with govt
summary: The PTI leader also described the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province as unconstitutional, alleging that the government had introduced the measures to take control of the provincial administration. “They just wanted to take over the province,” he said.

Deadlock on emergency and governor’s rule in K-P The debate over emergency and governor’s rule in K-P intensified in late September amid worsening security concerns and growing political tensions between the federal government and the PTI-led provincial administration.

On October 12, a petition challenging the imposition of emergency measures and governor’s rule in K-P was filed in the Peshawar High Court by PTI, a day after President Asif Ali Zardari approved the federal government’s decision on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

stories.title: Judi Dench says worsening eyesight means she can no longer act
summary: British actress Judi Dench said her eyesight had deteriorated to the point that she could no longer ​act on stage or in films.
Dench, 91, has had ‌macular degeneration for more than a decade "I can't be on stage, I can't do a play anymore, I can't do a film ​anymore, I can't read anymore," she told BBC Radio ​on Thursday.
Dench has had a seven-decade career on stage, ​film and television, receiving critical acclaim, including an Oscar, a ​Tony and seven Olivier awards.

stories.title: Zoya Nasir questions praise for Sacha Baron Cohen's Pakistan shoutout
summary: Actor Zoya Nasir questioned the excitement surrounding Hollywood comedian Sacha Baron Cohen’s recent shoutout to Pakistan, arguing that his history of comedy involving racial and religious stereotypes warranted a closer look at the interaction.
Cohen, dressed as his character for the upcoming film Ali G: Who Iz I, responds, “Yo, big up the Pakistan, man,” prompting cheers from people nearby.

Nasir’s comments highlight the divide in how Cohen’s comedy is received, particularly when an interaction involving one of his characters is interpreted as a gesture of goodwill towards a country or community.

stories.title: Canadian publisher says Thelyson Orelien used AI to write award-winning book, ends relationship
summary: Canadian publishing house Les Editions du Boreal said on Wednesday it had ended its professional relationship with Haitian-Canadian author Thelyson Orelien after it found that he had used Artificial Intelligence (AI) to write his award-winning book.

Orelien’s debut novel, C’etait ca ou mourir (It was either that or die), won a host of literary awards and was due to be translated into multiple languages before a little-known X account said last month that it was written almost entirely with AI.
Boreal said it would not reprint the novel or publish future works by Orelien.

stories.title: Apple will have limited iPhone Duo units available in stores on Friday
summary: Apple has said it will ​have 'limited' numbers of its folding iPhone Duo phone available ‌for walk-in customers when the device launches on Friday, after initial online orders sold out in minutes and pushed delivery times for some customers to January.

Read: India investigating Tata data leak that exposed Apple iPhone secrets “On Friday morning, our ​teams look forward to welcoming customers at Apple Stores to ​experience iPhone Duo and the incredible iPhone line-up for themselves," Apple said in a ‌statement.
In the China-governed territory of ​Macau, the iPhone Duo will be available for walk-in customers only, with limited inventory, ​Apple said.

stories.title: Govt directs ministries to compile civil servants' foreign nationality declarations
summary: Under Rule 3(3), civil servants must declare whether they hold the nationality of any foreign country, possess foreign travel documents or are married to a foreign national.

The prescribed format requires the name, designation and basic pay scale of each officer, confirmation of whether a declaration has been submitted under Rule 3(3), and details of the foreign nationality or travel-document status of both the officer and their dependants.
The Establishment Division, through an office memorandum, directed civil servants to provide details of foreign citizenship, foreign travel documents and marriages to foreign nationals.

stories.title: Suspects in West Bank settler attacks put under house arrest
summary: All but one of the suspects arrested over recent settler attacks on an American photojournalist and a visiting French mayor in the West Bank have been released from detention and placed under house arrest, their lawyers said.
The incident comes 10 days after settlers beat an AFP photographer covering the West Bank olive harvest, Jaafar Ashtiyeh, leaving him also requiring hospital treatment.
Violence has flared in recent months in the West Bank, with near-daily attacks, thefts or vandalism by Israeli settlers against Palestinians.

stories.title: DeepSeek wrapping up $15b fundraising to fuel AI race, sources say
summary: Chinese ​AI startup DeepSeek has raised about 100 billion yuan ($14.98 billion) in its latest funding round from investors including chipmaker ‌GigaDevice, food delivery company Meituan and automaker Geely, according to four people with knowledge of the matter.
On Thursday, Bloomberg first reported, citing sources, that DeepSeek had raised $15 billion in the latest funding round, with CATL and Tencent as its main backers.
Filings by two Chinese investors in July suggested DeepSeek was valued at ​350.88 billion yuan, or around $52 billion, in the June fundraising.

stories.title: Verstappen bids to delay Antonelli's F1 coronation
summary: Red Bull's four-time world champion won both the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia and then the Singapore Grand Prix to emerge as a leading contender for more success just when Mercedes' precocious 20-year-old Italian moved within reach of the title.

The 29-year-old Dutchman, who has acknowledged Antonelli's generational talent, won from pole at the Circuit of the Americas last year and is chasing a fifth win at the Texan track where Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton was won five times.
Antonelli was only four years old when Sebastian Vettel took the record as youngest champion, with Red Bull, in 2010, and he knows he must stay focused and race to win, as he always does.

stories.title: Pakistan whip Bhutan in tennis event
summary: Ushna Suhail and Mahin Aftab Qureshi secured straight-set victories in the singles before debutants Romaisa Malik and Hajra Sohail completed the clean sweep in doubles at the Pakistan Tennis Federation Tennis Complex.
Romaisa and Hajra then beat Bhutan's Kinley Yangden and Tandin Tsheyang Wangmo 6-1, 6-4 in their first appearance at the international team competition.
Pakistan will face Maldives on Friday as they continue their campaign in the women's international team tournament.

stories.title: Karachi court rejects Iqrarul Hassan's bail plea in anti-state content case
summary: The District and Sessions Court East dismissed a petition challenging Hassan's physical remand, with the defence counsel questioning the legality of the proceedings and arguing that the case concerned digital and cyber matters.
The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) registered the case against Hassan, who is currently in jail on judicial remand.
Last week, the NCCIA produced Hassan before the judicial magistrate, who granted a four-day physical remand.

stories.title: ATC replaces state counsel after Imaan, Hadi object to appointment
summary: Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra, who heard the case at Adiala Jail, accepted an application filed by Imaan and Hadi challenging Janjua’s appointment and appointed Atif Mahmood as the new state counsel.
Judge Sipra directed that they be summoned again on Friday. “Imaan and Hadi, if your lawyers do not cross-examine the witnesses tomorrow, the state counsel will do so,” the judge said.

The case so far The Islamabad ATC framed charges against Imaan and Hadi on October 7 in a case relating to the alleged removal of security barriers and disruption of a designated route during the visit of an international cricket team.

stories.title: President Zardari to visit Germany from Oct 22-24: FO
summary: Germany is Pakistan’s largest trading partner in the European Union, with both countries seeking to expand trade, investment and business cooperation.

Read: Maldives president arrives for three-day visit In August, German Consul General Thomas E Schultze highlighted the longstanding relationship and said economic cooperation between the two countries dated back to 1922, when Siemens opened its first office in Lahore.
In May, Pakistan and Germany signed a €40.5 million technical cooperation agreement covering nine new development projects, with support from Germany’s development bank, KfW.

stories.title: Pakistan, EU agree to boost counterterrorism cooperation, tackle online radicalisation: FO
summary: The two sides reviewed recent regional and global developments affecting the terrorism threat landscape and strongly condemned terrorism in all its forms, reaffirming their commitment to combating the threat.
The EU delegation condemned recent terrorist attacks in Pakistan, expressed solidarity with the victims and acknowledged Islamabad’s efforts to counter terrorism, the Foreign Office said.
The next round of the bilateral counterterrorism dialogue will be held in Brussels next year on a mutually convenient date, the Foreign Office said.

stories.title: Turkish foreign minister to host top diplomats in R4, R4+E3 meetings in Istanbul on Friday
summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan will host meetings of top diplomats of the R4 mechanism (Türkiye, Egypt, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia) and the European E3 mechanism (United Kingdom, Germany, and France), including in an unprecedented combined format, in Istanbul on Friday.

Fidan will likely reiterate that the dispute between the US and Iran can only be resolved through diplomacy and dialogue, stressing that military methods offer no lasting solution, exacerbate regional vulnerabilities, and carry the risk of a wider conflict.

The R4 mechanism was established by Türkiye, Egypt, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia on the basis of regional ownership, with the aim of supporting lasting stability and strengthening dialogue on regional issues.

stories.title: Noor Zaman stuns defending champion Gawad to reach Silicon Valley Open quarters
summary: Pakistan’s Noor Zaman stunned defending champion and world No. 4 Karim Abdel Gawad of Egypt 3-1 on Wednesday to reach the quarter-finals of the PSA Gold Silicon Valley Open at the Redwood City in California.
Noor, ranked among the world’s top 35 players, had earlier booked his place in the last 16 with a 3-1 victory over American wildcard Bransten Ming.
The PSA World Tour Gold event offers equal prize money for men and women as squash prepares for its Olympic debut at Los Angeles 2028.

stories.title: Lahore Gymkhana’s low rent attributed to ‘decades of oversight failures’
summary: Appearing before the committee alongside members of the club’s management, Mr Siddique expressed surprise at the nominal rate given the vast acreage involved and the club’s vastly improved financial footing.

Committee members noted that this admission from the club’s own top leadership underscored the urgency of determining why successive state authorities allowed such a massive concession to persist without meaningful scrutiny.
They stressed that the onus rested squarely on public institutions mandated to protect state land, enforce lease terms, and ensure transparent usage.

stories.title: Rawalpindi lawyers boycott courts over FIR against advocate for ‘assaulting’ judge
summary: RAWALPINDI: The contents of a sealed first information report (FIR) registered against an advocate for allegedly hitting a civil judge with a glass, injuring his head and fingers, in his chamber at the judicial complex on Tuesday have emerged.
Protesting against the registration of the FIR against the advocate, the Rawalpindi Bar Association boycotted court proceedings and staged a protest at the judicial complex on Wednesday.
The complainant added that when he and other court staff members tried to rescue the judge, Muhammad Farooq Aslam Khan and his companions assaulted him, causing him to fall to the ground.

stories.title: NAB seeks lowering of graft threshold to Rs50 million
summary: The NAB chairman claimed to have recovered state land worth trillions of rupees from encroachers, including 235,622 kanals of Pakistan Railways (PR).

Recovery claims According to NAB’s Director General (Operation) Amjad Aulakh, the bureau had retrieved state land worth Rs9.18 trillion in the third quarter of the current year, bringing the total recovery of the bureau to Rs11.524 trillion since 2023.

The NAB chairman said after making a record recovery of PR land, the bureau’s next target was to unveil corruption in the power sector, Evacuee Trust Property Board, state-owned enterprises, mines and minerals.

stories.title: Man sentenced to death for raping stepdaughter by Islamabad sessions court
summary: ISLAMABAD: An additional district and sessions court has sentenced a man to death for sexually assaulting his stepdaughter over a period of about a year, resulting in the birth of a child, and ordered him to pay Rs3 million in compensation to the victim and the child.
The court also ordered him to pay Rs1 million in damages to the victim and Rs2 million in compensation to the child born as a result of the assault.

According to the verdict, failure to pay the amount awarded to the victim would entail a further six months of imprisonment, while failure to pay the compensation awarded to the child would result in another six months behind bars.

stories.title: HSY to design new PIA cabin crew uniforms, set to debut on Oct 31
summary: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) has selected celebrated Pakistani couturier Hassan Sheheryar Yasin, popularly known as HSY, to design new uniforms for its cabin crew, with the collection set to debut on October 31, the national flag carrier announced on Thursday.

According to a statement issued by PIA, the collection aims to combine Pakistan’s cultural heritage with contemporary fashion while reflecting the airline’s emphasis on hospitality, passenger comfort and crew confidence.

The appointment brings a prominent name in Pakistani couture into the national carrier’s latest efforts to reshape its image while drawing on a fashion legacy that has linked PIA with internationally recognised designers for decades.

stories.title: Man flees after allegedly raping minor girl in Vehari
summary: BAHAWALPUR: A man allegedly raped a minor girl in Suleman Town in the limits of Burewala Saddar police precincts in Vehari district on Wednesday.
The girl, on returning home, informed her father about the incident, who reported the matter to Burewala Saddar police.
MURDER CASE ‘SOLVED’: Gaggo Mandi police claimed to have solved the blind murder case of a young girl, who was allegedly killed for “honour” by her father and his accomplices at Chak 229/WB.

stories.title: Peshawar High Court seeks govt response to petitions about school collapse
summary: PHCBA President Aminur Rehman Yousafzai and lawyer Fawad Jan appeared on behalf of the petitioners and told the court that the building of a private school, Al-Khair Education System, near Ring Road collapsed on Oct 15, killing 31 students and a teacher.

Citing information available in public reports, the petitioners claimed that the school building was not constructed or maintained according to approved plans, structural standards, fire-safety requirements and emergency exit regulations.

The counsel argued that the tragedy pointed to broader weaknesses in the regulatory framework governing school registration and inspection, approval and monitoring of building plans, land-use compliance and administrative oversight.
